name: Hydroxyethylrutosides (oxerutins)
short: Phlebotonics, class-wide (incl. rutosides): slightly more adverse events than placebo, mostly gut upsets. Review of 15 trials: no serious adverse effect reported. Pregnancy safety data are limited.
text: A 2020 Cochrane review of placebo-controlled trials of oral phlebotonics for chronic venous insufficiency (rutosides, hidrosmine and diosmine, calcium dobesilate, Centella asiatica, aminaftone, French maritime pine bark extract and grape seed extract; 28 of the 56 trials with usable efficacy data were on rutosides) pooled adverse events from 37 studies with 5789 participants and found that phlebotonics as a group probably increase adverse events slightly compared with placebo (risk ratio 1.14, 95% CI 1.02 to 1.27; moderate-certainty evidence), most often gastrointestinal disorders; only short-term safety data were available, and the abstract gives no figures for rutosides separately. A systematic review of 15 trials (1643 participants) of hydroxyethylrutosides, semisynthetic derivatives of rutin, for chronic venous insufficiency reported no serious adverse effect due to them, though all trials were of limited quality. In a Cochrane review of rutosides for post-thrombotic syndrome, mild side effects occurred in 7 of 41 people on rutosides and 5 of 42 on placebo or no treatment, and in another trial 6 of 80 stopped the medicine because of side effects. In pregnancy, a placebo-controlled trial of hydroxyethylrutosides taken by mouth in 97 women with haemorrhoids reported three mild, transient side effects and no drug-related problems in pregnancy or delivery, but a Cochrane review of treatments for varicose veins in pregnancy found too little data in its one rutoside trial (69 women) to assess safety in pregnancy. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
